sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Differential Diagnosis
sections.description: This section guides the reader through the patient's initial clinical picture, emphasizing the importance of timeline analysis and distinguishing between acute drug toxicity and progressive inflammatory myopathy.
subtopics: Patient demographics and baseline comorbidities (Obesity, NAFLD)
Initial acute toxicity after Semaglutide initiation (GI, Renal failure)
Evolution of symptoms: From acute reaction to subacute muscle weakness
Key physical exam findings: Proximal muscle weakness and dysphagia
Establishing the window of opportunity for early diagnosis

sections.description: This section provides essential background on IMNM, contrasting it with other myopathies and explaining the autoantibody profiles and mechanisms relevant to this specific case.
subtopics: Definition and histological hallmarks of IMNM (Necrosis vs. Inflammation)
Autoantibody associations: Anti-HMGCR and Anti-SRP
Traditional link between HMGCR and Statin therapy
The concept of seronegative IMNM and diagnostic challenges
Pathophysiological mechanisms of muscle fiber necrosis

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Biopsy, Serology, and Drug Causality
sections.description: This section dives into the diagnostic workup, explaining how to interpret muscle biopsies, serological limitations, and how to assess the causal link between medication and disease.
subtopics: Interpretation of CK trends and transaminase elevations
Muscle biopsy analysis: Macrophage infiltration and necrotic fibers
Limitations of the Myositis Antibody Panel in this context
Differentiating Drug-Induced Toxic Myopathy from Immunologic IMNM
Assessing Medication Causality using UMC Criteria

sections.description: This section outlines the therapeutic decisions made in the case, justifying the use of steroids and IVIG and discussing tapering strategies in a severe autoimmune context.
subtopics: Acute management: High-dose IV Methylprednisolone rationale
Indications for Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) in severe IMNM
Tapering inmunosuppression based on clinical response
Management of comorbidities (Septic shock considerations)
Discontinuation of the offending agent (Semaglutide)

sections.description: The final section synthesizes the outcome of the case, discusses long-term follow-up results, and highlights the broader implications for future prescribing of GLP-1 receptor agonists.
subtopics: Functional recovery and weaning from immunosuppression
Comparison with other reported cases of GLP-1 myopathy
Broader safety profile of GLP-1 agonists regarding muscle health
Importance of pharmacovigilance and reporting systems
Future monitoring recommendations for clinicians
